1.translation: After teaching in Chapters 7 and 8 that the Lord’s supreme truth is easily reached only through devotion, Śrīdhara now elaborates His inconceivable glory and the extraordinary power of devotion: “But to you, who do not find fault, I shall declare this most confidential knowledge together with realization. Knowing it, you will be freed from the inauspiciousness of saṃsāra and become liberated immediately.” Among progressively deeper teachings, knowledge of dharma is secret, knowledge of the Self distinct from the body is more secret, and knowledge of the Supreme Self is most secret.
word_for_word: in the seventh and eighth chapters
to one who does not find fault
knowledge of the Self distinct from the body and the rest

2.translation: This knowledge is the royal knowledge, the king among forms of knowledge; the royal secret, the king among what is hidden; supremely purifying; directly apprehended, with its result experienced immediately; righteous, because it is not separate from dharma and contains the fruits of all dharma; very easy to practice; and imperishable, because its fruit does not decay.
word_for_word: because it contains the fruit of all dharma

3.translation: Why, then, are there still people in saṃsāra if this teaching is so easy to practice? Those without faith in this dharma—who do not accept it with the attitude that it is true—even if they strive for attainment of Me by another means, fail to reach Me and return, wandering on the path of death-filled saṃsāra.
word_for_word: not accepting it with an attitude of trust
